boxes.comments: The two U forms have open hooked upper-left entries; two separate equality bars and a low S are visible. In schéma the acute is detached above e, and the last a is a tiny dark rounded body with an internal light opening and short terminal return. No independent period is secured. Clipped neighboring fragments are excluded.

Both ends of élémentaire carry paired raised quotation ticks. Both e accents are retained. The text continues sur and a tall S, followed by one detached horizontal dash. The triple hyphen is the textual encoding of that one dash.

After live lui and a separate hyphen, the final abbreviation consists of a low m-like cup/cusp body with a separate straight upper bar. The abbreviation is retained without expansion and without assigning a mathematical role. No terminal stop is secured.

Long horizontal top bar over two essentially straight descending strokes; the second descends obliquely, with no secure curled foot. The isolated short stroke at lower right reads subscript 1. Capital Pi is the present graphical preference, but lowercase pi remains locally uncertain. This crop was reopened once to inspect the alphabet form. It is an inline expression, not a formula or page label.
Detached upper short bar and main descending angled stroke with a low bowl/hook read 5. A separate dark period follows. It is a prose reference number, with no surrounding parentheses.

The raised variable has a tall upper stem/hook, a short rightward middle arm, and a lower leftward hook: f is preferred, with s retained as a graphical alternative. A separate curved leader runs down-left from beside the raised glyph to the gap before live de, after the preceding clipped word. Both leader ends were traced on the crop and original. The clipped preceding word is excluded; no deletion is visible.

Full expression reads E with subscript U and a further low eta. The last character has a left upright, rising bridge/arch, and right descending hooked return; no separate lower angled K arm is secured. U has an open upper entry. No additional accent or punctuation is supplied.

Central nested addition is la section. Its caret/leader points after de in the lower parenthesis and before the first E-eta expression. The higher de belongs to the main line above, not to this nested addition. The broad lower line belongs to the outer parenthetical attachment, rather than underlining or cancellation. The partly clipped neighboring formula is read in full in B09/B11 and is not completed here.

Full added parenthesis and both morphisms are recorded. Nested la section attaches between composé de and the first E-eta expression. The outer underbrace-like attachment has a downward notch pointing to the gap after the baseline E_K to E_US expression and before Je; both endpoints were traced in the broad box and original. Source of the second morphism has a nested K with angled arms, while the first morphism has eta. Short connecting lines have hooked/angled right terminals but uncertain complete arrowheads; right-arrow versus literal horizontal stroke is retained locally. The long descenders from surjectif above overlap the added formula and are not cancellation marks. A tiny detached dark point near original (1623,1597), above the right end of the brace and lower-left of the closing parenthesis, is retained as a doubtful point: punctuation status, scope, and serial placement remain unresolved. Main-line words above and clipped baseline expressions below are excluded from the added text.

The full abbreviation has l with a low turn, a distinct apostrophe, h with tall stem/shoulder, a small o body, and a low m with a long flat terminal return. No detached terminal point is visible. No expansion is supplied.

Full first morphism of the outer insertion: E_eta to E_U_eta. The short shaft has a dark angled/downward hook at its right, but a complete arrowhead is not securely separated; right arrow is preferred with horizontal-stroke alternative. The caret from the nested la section overlaps the upper-left vicinity of the first E. The lower long line is the outer attachment mark, not an underline.

Full second morphism of the outer insertion and its closing parenthesis: E_U_K to E_U_S. The low K has two angled arms; target S has upper curve and lower return. The shaft/right terminal are partly overlapped by the long j descender in surjectif above; a single right arrow is preferred but a horizontal stroke remains possible. The large curved stroke around the target comes from the f descender above and is not treated as cancellation. The small detached point below-left of the closing parenthesis has uncertain punctuation state and scope, as described in B09. U entries are open.

The full live baseline morphism has source E_eta and target E_S. The shaft ends in a small dark angular thickening/hook followed by one separately visible complete greater-than-shaped head. A single-headed arrow is preferred; the shaft-end thickening may be an additional head or terminal pen motion, so the two-headed alternative remains local. No arrow count is inferred from neighboring prose.

Read literally defini: d oval/ascender, compressed e, long f with lower loop, two dotted i forms, low internal n, and short rightward terminal return. No separate acute is securely visible over the first e. The faint speck much higher above that position is not enough to supply an accent. No separate final e or terminal punctuation is secured. Spelling is retained without normalization.

The central canceled word following live section is heavily crossed by horizontal ink. An initial s-like curved form survives at the left; the middle has shallow cup/return fragments and the right retains a short rising shoulder/return. Tentative sur is recorded as a whole-word doubt, with the internal letters substantially obscured. The strike extends through the entire tentative word; live section is contextual and excluded from this row. A small raised slant at the end of that preceding live word is visible, but its attachment/state is unresolved and is not supplied as a definite punctuation mark. The first attempted display of this saved crop was truncated by the tool; it was reopened successfully without recreating the crop.

Full expression reads E_U_eta sur E_K. First E is two-lobed; open-entry U carries a lower eta with rising bridge and right descending return. The word sur is live and complete. The final K has a long upper diagonal and a distinct lower angled arm. No bar, hat, equality sign, or final punctuation is supplied.

Separate small lower-left marginal foliation reads 69: 6 has an upper rising stroke and closed lower loop; 9 has a closed upper loop and long downward leftward terminal stroke. Retained as margin rather than head page number.

independence_attestation: I had not read this page in the first pass. I used only the generic blind-reader contract, the assigned original scan, the frozen box list, and the fresh crops made from that original. I opened no witnesses, first readings, page transcriptions, reviews, notes, notation lists, packets, other pages, or comparison files. Every prescribed crop was visually inspected directly. No OCR or text-recognition software was used.
method: Each frozen rectangle was cropped once from the original, enlarged to 2800 pixels wide with LANCZOS, autocontrasted, and mildly sharpened with UnsharpMask(radius=1.2, percent=110, threshold=3). All rotations are 0 degrees. The original was viewed for layout and reopened for context of the final canceled passage; B04 was reopened to inspect the alphabet form. B15 initially failed to display because its tool result was truncated, then the same saved crop was reopened successfully. No crops were recreated.
return_policy: The TSV is fixed before reporting. No comparison was performed by this reader, and the returned files will remain unchanged.
